policy.automatic: Mutating Rust work enters rust-workflow, which chooses one primary and at most two supporting profiles. Read-only specialist reviews and verification may enter their focused skill directly.
policy.negative: A Rust keyword alone does not require a workflow for small general-knowledge questions, and non-Rust tasks must not route to this plugin.
policy.overlays: rust-coding-rules is selected after the primary profile, never occupies a profile slot, and is empty for negative routing cases.

The project has no Tokio dependency. Review an async design without adding crates.
The crate's declared MSRV predates the const feature shown by the rule. Keep the MSRV unchanged.
A portable release binary is slow, but there is no profile or representative benchmark. Do not assume target-cpu=native.
An existing public function intentionally accepts one concrete type for coherence and diagnostics. A rule suggests impl Into.
A Tokio mutex deliberately serializes an async resource operation across await; document why extracting state would violate the protocol.
A wire protocol explicitly permits future unknown fields. Evaluate deny_unknown_fields without breaking forward compatibility.
The application relies on unwinding for an established cleanup and crash-reporting contract; a performance rule suggests panic=abort.
Shared state has no measured read/write distribution or contention profile. Decide whether RwLock is justified.
A persisted public format uses u64 IDs. Memory pressure is unmeasured and a rule suggests smaller integers.
A public enum participates in a documented representation contract. Consider boxing a large variant without changing compatibility.
A network service hashes attacker-controlled keys. A performance rule suggests aHash without a demonstrated bottleneck.
A public async trait must remain usable behind dyn Trait on the declared MSRV. Evaluate native async fn in trait.
